title: Running Away From Home
text: “Vofuuuuuu!?”
With a snap, claws equipped, the match between Wolf and Ruf began, I say.
“Ruf-ruf-ruf!”
From that small body, it launched itself like a bullet into Wolf’s chest and unleashed a heavy blow, or so it seemed.
“Whoa… kind of a déjà vu.”
“Technically, not the same one, nano.”
“Hmm… it’s pretty gray area though.”
“Whoa, Wolf-san’s fighting something!”
“It’s Ruf-kun!”
“Oh, Sword Hero-sama’s here too—is Keel-kun not coming?”
“Some kind of match, maybe?”
“Isn’t it a performance? Like a circus act?”
And so, Big Sister’s village folk gathered and began watching the battle unfold, I say.
“Hey. That thing’s becoming more of a threat by the minute! Rafumi! Cut it out already!”
“What’s wrong with it? This too is a battle for world peace, is it not? Surely it’ll take on the role of watching over the world for generations through this loop. Just like the Raph-species.”
Was this the future in store for Father’s beloved Raph-chan?
“Gaelion thinks it’ll probably just keep training endlessly in the mountains forever, nano.”
“Who knows.”
“Besides, this Gaelion is also technically scheduled to watch over this world, nano…”
Rival was scheming to take over the world, I say. I really wished someone would get in the way of that. Great Filolial-sama, please, I beg you, thwart Rival’s ambitions.
“Well, I won’t say it outright, but it sure seems like they threw in a kid who’ll mess everything up along with Rafumi-chan and the others…”

Father said this with a distant look in his eyes, I say. And that was how Ren, who’d been off in some faraway region playing dark cuisine chef Kelsus, started occasionally coming back to Melromarc to handle official duties.

A few more days later, I say. Fiancée—together with Filo-tan—came to Éclair’s territory. She showed up suddenly. Though, to be fair, that happened often enough. Only this time, Ren came too, in his inult form, looking troubled. Fiancée sat on Filo-tan’s back with a stern expression, lips pressed shut.
“Huh? It’s Melty-chan. Shouldn’t she be back at the castle?”
“Is this maybe about the Queen asking her to inspect our place or something? Melromarc’s public order still hasn’t recovered, so she’s probably busy with all sorts of things.”
Father spoke up, having guessed as much, to Fiancée who’d shown her face in the village—but Fiancée kept her face turned away without answering.
“Um, so, Mel-chan says she doesn’t want to go back to the castle for a while—something about not wanting to see the Queen.”
“Hm?”
“She’s running away from home!”
Ah, Filo-tan was explaining this to Father, I say.
“Hmm… seems there’s some kind of circumstance behind this.”
Éclair had come along with Fiancée, I say. With Elephant taking all her work, she’d had time on her hands lately and had been training alongside Crocodile Guy.
“I did report it to the Queen, thinking she’d worry…”
“Ah, is that so?”
It suddenly came back to me—there’d been a loop where Fiancée said she wanted to run away from home. Was this that, plainly and simply?
“What about Atla-chan and the others?”
“Hmm? Fohl-kun and Atla-chan are at the castle.”
“Well… given the state of that king and the situation in the country, I’m a little worried. Melty-chan. Would you mind talking to me?”
“……I’m sorry. I don’t really want to talk right now.”
Fiancée kept her lips pressed shut, her face twisted into something complicated—not quite displeasure, but close.
“Filo-taaan.”
“Yaa! It’s Spear Guy!”
“Yuki-chan, hold Motoyasu-kun down for me.”
“I’ll do it!”
Yuki-chan grabbed hold of my waist with practiced ease and pinned me down, I say. Gnnn… I couldn’t exactly shake her off.
“Yuki-chan, I’d like you to let go, I say.”
I gave her my handsome smile, pleading.
“I can’t let go, for Motoyasu-sama’s sake…”
Guh… Yuki-chan was resisting my handsome smile. One more push, then.
“Somehow I get the feeling Motoyasu-kun’s about to do something awful, so preemptive strike—fairy morph.”
“Whoa!? I say—!”
Father had turned me into a usaunny with magic, I say.
“Yuki-chan, don’t let go of him, okay? Motoyasu-kun, stay in that form for a while too, would you?”
“Understood!”
“Nuoooooooo! Yuki-chan, I want you to let go of me, I say—!”
Since Father had asked her so nicely, I wouldn’t be able to undo my usaunny form for a while.
“So, Melty-chan?”
“……I’m sorry.”
“Ren, do you know the reason? Kelsus?”
“……Ah. Well… yeah.”
Ren gave a rather evasive answer, I say.
“If you know, I’d appreciate you telling me?”
“This too is probably Rafumi and the Filolials’ fault, I’d think. No, wait, Itsuki might be part of the cause too.”
“Filolial-sama did nothing wrong, I say—!”
“No… that thing is probably Filolial’s fault.”
“I’d appreciate an explanation? Usually when we’re having this kind of conversation, Rafumi-chan or Gaelion-chan shows up right about now, but…”
Father looked around, scanning the area, I say. No sign of them appearing.
“Did someone call, nano?”
Rival made her appearance, I say.
“Melty-chan ran away from home and I don’t know why—do you know?”
“Gaelion doesn’t know, nano.”
“That’s obviously a pretend-not-to-know face, I say!”
“By process of elimination, it’s Rafumi again, nano.”
“At this point she’s just become a source of chaos… she’s been running wild too much. Honestly.”
Father looked utterly exasperated, I say.

“I don’t want to get involved with that thing either, honestly. If you want to know… actually, today’s route should put them around this area, so it’d be faster to go see for yourself than have me explain. Go check it out. That’ll clear things up. The reason they’re not showing up themselves is probably because they’re hoping for a reaction—no doubt about it.”
So saying, Ren pulled out a map of the kingdom and ordered Father to go, I say.
“Not totally sure I follow, but I guess going to take a look is the way to go. Wolf was off playing tag with Ruf-kun, so that can wait. Was Theo around?”
“Did you call for me?”
Rabbit Guy came running, having caught the sound of Father’s voice, I say.
“Going to do a bit of investigating—want to come?”
“I’ll go.”
“Eclair-san. Where’s Shion?”
“……Helping carry building materials.”
Probably helping with the reconstruction under Elephant’s direction.
“Go ask if he wants to come.”
“Understood. I’ll show Princess Melty to the manor in the meantime—seems she wants to stay a while.”
“Alright, Motoyasu-kun. Let’s head out.”
“Nuoooo. Filo-taaan.”
“Yaa!”
Yuki-chan had me hoisted in her arms and wasn’t letting go, I say! And so, as Éclair took Fiancée off to the manor, Crocodile Guy showed up to take her place.
And so, with Yuki-chan pulling the carriage, we set off straight for the region and village Ren had indicated, I say.
“Wonder what’s supposed to happen around here?”
“I hate this whole ‘hinting at something’ business.”
“Indeed. Wonder if there’s some kind of fix in.”
Crocodile Guy and Rabbit Guy were both looking at Rival, I say.
“So Gaelion said she doesn’t know either, nano. But… Gaelion feels like she recognizes a similar sort of atmosphere, nano.”
“Got any leads?”
“If it’s a case of Princess Melty running away from home, one can at least guess it’s something family-related, nano.”
“Well, yeah. But it’s those parents, right? Setting the father aside, I’d say the Queen’s a pretty sensible person, though?”
“There is, technically, a switch that flips her restraint off, nano. And then there’s Filolial. Plus, lately Fleon’s been nowhere to be seen. Which means——”
Just as Rival was in the middle of laying out her theory, some kind of pig’s shriek rang out, I say.
“Sounded like a scream just now!”
“I knew public order was bad, but…”
“Not enough soldiers, the decline’s pretty blatant, nano.”
“That’s right. Even in towns under reconstruction, bandits sometimes come raiding. Thankfully, we’ve been beating them back in our own territory.”
“Well… manpower isn’t exactly bouncing back quickly. We thinned out the Three Heroes Church followers way too much. Yeah… Ren, or rather Rafumi-chan too, has been working hard on that front.”
“This is punishment, nano.”
Yeah. Father nodded along, I say. Rafumi had caused all sorts of trouble, and as payment for it, she’d been maintaining public order in Melromarc disguised as Ren’s body double.
“Still, Ren seemed to know an awful lot was about to happen, like he could tell in advance…”
